work: Enarratio in Epistolam II B. Pauli ad Thessalonicenses
source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. XIII (Montreuil)

1.title: EXPOSITIO PRIMI CAPITULI : PAULUS ET SILVANUS ET TIMOTHEUS ECCLESIÆ THESSALONICENSIUM.
1.title_en: Exposition of the first chapter: Paul and Silvanus and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians.

paras.t: PAULUS et Silvanus et Timotheus, Ecclesiæ Thessalonicensium, in Deo Patre nostro et Domino Jesu Christo, etc. Omnia verba hæc in exordio epistolæ præcedentis exposita sunt. Nam et verbo et sensu idem est utriusque epistolæ principium.
paras.en: [[1:1|Paul and Sylvanus and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians. In God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ|PAULUS et Silvanus et Timotheus, Ecclesiæ Thessalonicensium, in Deo Patre nostro et Domino Jesu Christo]], etc. All these words have been expounded at the opening of the preceding epistle[[1 Thess 1:1||]]. For the beginning of both epistles is the same, in word and in sense.

paras.t: Gratias agere debemus Deo semper, id est omni tempore congruenti, pro vobis, id est propter beneficia vobis divinitus præstita, o fratres : ad hoc enim tenemur tanquam pastores vestri. Caritas quoque qua de vestra salute gaudemus et Dei honorem concupimus, ad hanc nos gratiarum actionem constringit. Ita ut dignum est, id est multum affectuose atque humiliter, sicut pro tantis beneficiis, tanto benefactori a tantillis gratias agi decet. Quoniam supercrescit, id est, plurimum proficit, fides vestra : nam per illuminationem Spiritus Sancti fit clarior, atque per opera bona vivacior ; et abundat caritas uniuscujusque vestrum in invicem, id est, unusquisque vestrum alium amat ferventer spirituali et sancta dilectione :
paras.en: [[1:3|We are bound to give thanks always to God|Gratias agere debemus Deo semper]], that is, at every fitting time, [[1:3|for you|pro vobis]], that is, on account of the benefits divinely bestowed on you, O [[1:3|brethren|fratres]]: for to this we are bound as your shepherds. The charity too, by which we rejoice in your salvation and long for God's honour, constrains us to this thanksgiving. [[1:3|as it is fitting|Ita ut dignum est]], that is, with great affection and humility, as it is fitting that thanks be given by such little ones to so great a benefactor for such great benefits. [[1:3|because your faith groweth exceedingly|quoniam supercrescit fides vestra]], that is, makes very great progress: for by the illumination of the Holy Ghost it becomes clearer, and by good works more lively; [[1:3|and the charity of every one of you towards each other aboundeth|et abundat caritas uniuscujusque vestrum in invicem]], that is, each one of you loves the other fervently with a spiritual and holy love:

paras.t: ita ut et nos ipsi in vobis, id est de vestra perfectione, vel in perfectionis vestræ consideratione, gloriemur in Ecclesiis Dei, id est coram congregationibus Christianorum, ad quorum ædificationem lætanter referimus vestras virtutes : gloriemur, inquam, pro, id est de, patientia vestra et fide, quæ fortiter conservastis in omnibus persecutionibus vestris, quæ extrinsecus infliguntur, et tribulationibus aliis, quas sustinetis, in exemplum, id est in declarationem, justi judicii Dei futuri in morte cujuslibet, vel in die novissimo. Tribulationes quippe quas sustinetis, testantur et manifestant quod Deus post hanc vitam judicat patientes et inferentes, reddens singulis quod merentur, videlicet patientibus gloriam. Qui enim humiliatus fuerit, erit in gloria. Quum namque cernamus in hac vita impios prosperari et justos opprimere, justos autem adversitatibus fatigari et opprimi etiam usque ad mortem, oportet concedere quod justus et sapiens Deus post hanc vitam omnia recte disponat, juste judicet, et optime ordinet : quod non fit nisi per justam damnationem malorum et beatificationem justorum. Ut digni, id est gloriosi, habeamini (vel, Digni habeamini, id est, digni sitis per opera sancta recipi) in regno Dei, id est Ecclesia triumphanti ac throno cœlesti, pro quo, videlicet ut sic digni habeamini, et patimini tanta adversa, pensantes illud Evangelii : Gaudete in illa hora et exsultate, ecce enim merces vestra copiosa est in cœlis. Si enim compatimur, et conregnabimus.
paras.en: [[1:4|So that we ourselves also glory in you|ita ut et nos ipsi in vobis]], that is, of your perfection, or in considering your perfection, [[1:4|glory in you in the churches of God|gloriemur in Ecclesiis Dei]], that is, before the congregations of Christians, to whose edification we joyfully report your virtues: we glory, I say, [[1:4|for|pro]], that is, about, [[1:4|your patience and faith|patientia vestra et fide]], which you have bravely kept [[1:4|in all your persecutions|in omnibus persecutionibus vestris]], which are inflicted from without, [[1:4|and tribulations|et tribulationibus]] of other kinds, [[1:4|which you endure|quas sustinetis]], [[1:5|For an example|in exemplum]], that is, for a declaration, [[1:5|of the just judgment of God|justi judicii Dei]] to come at each one's death, or on the last day. For the tribulations you endure testify and make plain that God, after this life, judges those who suffer and those who inflict, rendering to each what he deserves, namely glory to those who suffer. For he that hath been humbled shall be in glory[[Job 22:29||]] [no margin reference is printed; the words are those of Job 22:29]. For since we see in this life the wicked prospering and oppressing the just, and the just wearied by adversities and oppressed even unto death, we must grant that the just and wise God after this life disposes all things rightly, judges justly and orders them most well: which comes about only through the just damnation of the wicked and the beatification of the just. [[1:5|that you may be counted worthy|ut digni habeamini]] [Denis's text reads *habeamini*, “we may be counted”], that is, glorious (or, “be counted worthy”, that is, be worthy through holy works to be received) [[1:5|of the kingdom of God|in regno Dei]], that is, into the Church triumphant and the heavenly throne, [[1:5|for which|pro quo]], namely that you may thus be counted worthy, [[1:5|also you suffer|et patimini]] such great adversities, weighing that word of the Gospel: [[Luke 6:23|Be glad in that day and rejoice: for behold, your reward is great in heaven|Gaudete in illa hora et exsultate, ecce enim merces vestra copiosa est in cœlis]][[Matt 5:12||]]. For if we suffer with him, we shall also reign with him[[Rom 8:17||]][[2 Tim 2:12||]].

paras.t: Si tamen, id est quia, justum est apud Deum, id est, in mente divina hoc justum censetur, retribuere tribulationem his qui vos tribulant, id est persecutoribus vestris debitas reddere pœnas pro pœnis quas vobis infligunt. Quod utique justum est et continget, sicut et Psalmista testatur : Qui custodit veritatem in sæculum, facit judicium injuriam patientibus. Unde et in Job habetur : Deus inultum abire non patitur. Justum quoque est apud Deum, et vobis qui tribulamini propter justitiam, requiem dare æternam nobiscum in patria. Ideo namque in libro Sapientiæ legimus : Deus tentavit illos, et invenit illos dignos se; ideoque accipient regnum decoris, et diadema speciei de manu Domini. Et in Apocalypsi : Isti sunt qui venerunt de tribulatione magna, ideo sunt ante thronum Dei.
paras.en: [[1:6|Seeing|Si tamen]], that is, because, [[1:6|it is a just thing with God|justum est apud Deum]], that is, in the divine mind this is judged just, [[1:6|to repay tribulation to them that trouble you|retribuere tribulationem his qui vos tribulant]], that is, to render to your persecutors the penalties due for the pains they inflict on you. Which surely is just and will come to pass, as the Psalmist also testifies: [[Ps 145:7|Who keepeth truth for ever: who executeth judgment for them that suffer wrong|Qui custodit veritatem in sæculum, facit judicium injuriam patientibus]] [the Douay-Rheims divides this between Ps 145:6 and 7]. Hence in Job too it is said: God doth not suffer it to go unrevenged[[Job 24:12||]]. It is just also with God [[1:7|And to you who are troubled|et vobis qui tribulamini]] for justice' sake, to give [[1:7|rest|requiem]] eternal [[1:7|with us|nobiscum]] in the fatherland. For this reason we read in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 3:5|God hath tried them, and found them worthy of himself|Deus tentavit illos, et invenit illos dignos se]]; [[Wis 5:17|Therefore shall they receive a kingdom of glory, and a crown of beauty at the hand of the Lord|ideoque accipient regnum decoris, et diadema speciei de manu Domini]]. And in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 7:14|These are they who are come out of great tribulation|Isti sunt qui venerunt de tribulatione magna]], therefore they are before the throne of God[[Apoc 7:15||]] [the margin gives Apoc. vii, 14, 15].

paras.t: Hæc autem retributio plenarie fiet, et justum est apud Deum eam compleri, in revelatione, id est manifesta apparitione, Domini Jesu venientis de cœlo in die novissimo, cum angelis virtutis ejus, id est angelis sanctis suæ divinæ potestati, imo et suæ humanitati subjectis ; in flamma ignis dantis vindictam, id est in revelatione Jesu dantis in flamma ignis, id est per ignem flammantem, vindictam, id est justam ultionem, iis qui non noverunt Deum scientia formata quæ facit quod novit agendum, id est injustis, qui etsi dicant se nosse Deum, factis negant. De hac enim scientia ait Joannes in prima sua Canonica : Qui dicit se nosse Deum, et mandata ejus non custodit, mendax est. Vel per ignorantes Deum, intelliguntur idololatræ. Et iis qui non obediunt Evangelio, id est evangelicæ doctrinæ, Domini nostri Jesu Christi. De hac Christi revelatione et flamma ignis psaltes David clarissime prophetavit : Deus manifeste veniet, Deus noster, et non silebit ; ignis in conspectu ejus exardescet.
paras.en: Now this retribution will be made in full, and it is just with God that it be fulfilled, [[1:7|when the Lord Jesus shall be revealed|in revelatione Domini Jesu]], that is, at the manifest appearing of the Lord Jesus, coming [[1:7|from heaven|de cœlo]] on the last day, [[1:7|with the angels of his power|cum angelis virtutis ejus]], that is, with the holy angels subject to his divine power, nay, to his humanity as well; [[1:8|In a flame of fire, giving vengeance|in flamma ignis dantis vindictam]], that is, at the revelation of Jesus giving in a flame of fire, that is, through flaming fire, vengeance, that is, just requital, [[1:8|to them who know not God|iis qui non noverunt Deum]] with formed knowledge [that is, knowledge informed by charity], which does what it knows ought to be done; that is, to the unjust, who though they say they know God, in their works deny him[[Tit 1:16||]]. For of this knowledge John says in his first Canonical epistle: [[1 John 2:4|He who saith that he knoweth him and keepeth not his commandments is a liar|Qui dicit se nosse Deum, et mandata ejus non custodit, mendax est]]. Or by those ignorant of God are meant idolaters. [[1:8|and who obey not the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ|Et iis qui non obediunt Evangelio, id est evangelicæ doctrinæ, Domini nostri Jesu Christi]], that is, the gospel teaching. Of this revelation of Christ and flame of fire the psalmist David most clearly prophesied: [[Ps 49:3|God shall come manifestly: our God shall come, and shall not keep silence. A fire shall burn before him|Deus manifeste veniet, Deus noster, et non silebit ; ignis in conspectu ejus exardescet]].

paras.t: Qui nescientes et inobedientes, pœnas dabunt, id est persolvent et luent, in interitu æternas, id est æternaliter perdurantes, et quasi occidentes, non tamen exstinguentes, eos quos punient. Unde hæ pœnæ sunt mors secunda, æterna et amarissima. Has igitur pœnas dabunt, id est, sustinebunt sibi inflictas, a facie Domini, id est a præsentia Christi, qui dicet : Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum. Cujus facies reprobis erit horrenda ac pœnalissima, ita ut dicant montibus et petris : Cadite super nos, et abscondite nos a facie Sedentis super thronum, et ab ira Agni. Et a gloria virtutis ejus, id est ab excellentia seu majestate potentiæ Christi, qui in suo imperio reprobos in pœnas inferni detrudet. Data namque est ei omnis potestas in cœlo et in terra.
paras.en: [[1:9|Who|Qui]], ignorant and disobedient, [[1:9|shall suffer eternal punishment in destruction|pœnas dabunt, in interitu æternas]] [*pœnas dabunt*, literally “shall pay penalties”], that is, shall pay and atone, eternal punishments, that is, lasting eternally, and as it were slaying, yet not extinguishing, those whom they punish. Hence these punishments are the second death[[Apoc 21:8||]], eternal and most bitter. These punishments, then, they shall pay, that is, endure as inflicted on them, [[1:9|from the face of the Lord|a facie Domini]], that is, from the presence of Christ, who will say: [[Matt 25:41|Depart from me, you cursed, into everlasting fire|Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum]]. His face will be dreadful and most painful to the reprobate, so that they will say to the mountains and the rocks: [[Apoc 6:16|Fall upon us and hide us from the face of him that sitteth upon the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb|Cadite super nos, et abscondite nos a facie Sedentis super thronum, et ab ira Agni]]. [[1:9|and from the glory of his power|Et a gloria virtutis ejus]], that is, from the excellence or majesty of the might of Christ, who by his command will thrust the reprobate down into the pains of hell. For [[Matt 28:18|All power is given to me in heaven and in earth|omnis potestas in cœlo et in terra]] has been given to him.

paras.t: Quum venerit Christus glorificari, id est glorificatus atque magnificus apparere, in Sanctis suis, id est in præmiatione seu glorificatione electorum suorum ; et quum venerit admirabilis fieri in cordibus omnium intuentium in omnibus qui crediderunt, id est in justa retributione seu præmio universorum fidelium, bonos salvando, impiosque damnando. Ex quo effectu cunctis patebit quam admirabilis sit Dominus Jesus, quemadmodum scriptum est : Mirabilis Deus in Sanctis suis. Signum vero quod omnia ista sic fient, est : Quia creditum est testimonium nostrum, id est, attestatio seu prædicatio nostra de justo judicio Dei credita est, super vos, id est a vobis vel in cordibus vestris. Hoc enim sensu in Isaia habetur : Spiritus Domini super me, id est in me. Creditum est in die illo, id est, sic quod complebitur in die novissimo, quando omnes simul remunerabuntur ; vel, In die illo, id est de die illo, quia de die judicii credidistis quæ prædicavimus vobis.
paras.en: [[1:10|When he shall come to be glorified|Quum venerit Christus glorificari]], Christ, that is, to appear glorified and magnificent, [[1:10|in his saints|in Sanctis suis]], that is, in the rewarding or glorifying of his elect; and when he shall come [[1:10|to be made wonderful|admirabilis fieri]] in the hearts of all who behold, [[1:10|in all them who have believed|in omnibus qui crediderunt]], that is, in the just requital or reward of all the faithful, saving the good and damning the wicked. From which effect it will be plain to all how wonderful the Lord Jesus is, as it is written: [[Ps 67:36|God is wonderful in his saints|Mirabilis Deus in Sanctis suis]]. And the sign that all these things will so come to pass is this: [[1:10|because our testimony was believed|Quia creditum est testimonium nostrum]], that is, our attestation or preaching about the just judgment of God has been believed, [[1:10|upon you|super vos]], that is, by you, or in your hearts. For in this sense it is said in Isaias: [[Is 61:1|The spirit of the Lord is upon me|Spiritus Domini super me]], that is, in me. It was believed [[1:10|in that day|in die illo]], that is, in such wise that it will be fulfilled on the last day, when all will be rewarded together; or, “in that day”, that is, about that day, because you believed what we preached to you about the day of judgment.

paras.t: In quo negotio seu testimonio prædicationis nostræ, etiam oramus semper pro vobis, ut dignetur, id est, dignos efficiat, vos vocatione sua, id est beatitudine ad quam vocati estis, Deus noster, et impleat omnem voluntatem bonitatis suæ, id est, quidquid suæ pietati placitum est, ad effectum perducat in vobis, quatenus faciat vos suis præceptis atque consiliis misericorditer datis obedire in omnibus. Impleat quoque et opus fidei, id est opera virtuosa ex fide nascentia, sine quibus fides mortua est in se ipsa. Vel, opus fidei proprie intelligitur oris confessio, qua quis fidem profitetur. Corde enim creditur ad justitiam, ore vero confessio fit ad salutem. Quæ confessio summe necessaria fuit martyribus tempore Apostolorum, et postmodum diu. In virtute constantiæ seu animi firmitate, vel fortiter, stetis, atque in finem perseveretis.
paras.en: [[1:11|Wherefore|In quo]] [literally “in which”], that is, in which business or testimony of our preaching, [[1:11|also we pray always for you|etiam oramus semper pro vobis]], [[1:11|That our God would make you worthy|ut dignetur]], that is, may make you worthy, [[1:11|of his vocation|vos vocatione sua]], that is, of the beatitude to which you have been called, [[1:11|our God|Deus noster]], [[1:11|and fulfil all the good pleasure of his goodness|et impleat omnem voluntatem bonitatis suæ]], that is, may bring to effect in you whatever is pleasing to his kindness, so as to make you obey in all things his precepts and counsels mercifully given. May he fulfil also [[1:11|the work of faith|et opus fidei]], that is, the virtuous works born of faith, without which faith is dead in itself[[Jas 2:20||]]. Or, the work of faith is properly understood as the confession of the mouth by which one professes the faith. [[Rom 10:10|For, with the heart, we believe unto justice: but, with the mouth, confession is made unto salvation|Corde enim creditur ad justitiam, ore vero confessio fit ad salutem]]. This confession was supremely necessary for the martyrs in the time of the Apostles and for long afterwards. [[1:11|in power|In virtute]] of constancy, or firmness of soul, or bravely, that you may stand and persevere to the end.

paras.t: Ut clarificetur nomen Domini nostri Jesu Christi, id est, ipse Christus clarificetur, in vobis dupliciter : Primo, ut eum sincere cognoscatis, et digne honoretis. Sic enim clarificatur, id est, clare habetur, scitur et honoratur in cordibus vestris. De tali clarificatione ait Salvator : Pater, venit hora, clarifica Filium tuum. Secundo, ut divina perfectio Christi in vobis appareat, et ita Christus in vobis per suum præclarum effectum innotescat seu declaretur. Et vos in illo, id est, in Christo clarificemini, videndo eum in patria facie ad faciem. Non ergo eodem modo clarificatur Christus in nobis, et nos in illo. Per hoc enim quod ipse clarificatur in nobis, nihil perfectionis aut gloriæ ei accrescit; per hoc autem quod nos clarificamur in Christo, summe perficimur. Sic igitur clarificemini in illo, secundum gratiam Dei nostri, id est juxta mensuram gratiæ vobis a sancta Trinitate exhibitæ, et Domini Jesu Christi, id est secundum eamdem gratiam, quæ nobis per Christum tanquam per mediatorem et causam meritoriam datur. Hoc dicit Apostolus, ne quis propriis meritis principaliter innitatur.
paras.en: [[1:12|That the name of our Lord Jesus|Ut clarificetur nomen Domini nostri Jesu Christi]] [*clarificetur*, “be made bright, glorified”], that is, that Christ himself may be glorified, [[1:12|may be glorified in you|in vobis]] in two ways: first, that you may know him sincerely and honour him worthily. For so he is glorified, that is, is held clearly, known and honoured in your hearts. Of such glorification the Saviour says: [[John 17:1|said: the hour is come. Glorify thy Son|Pater, venit hora, clarifica Filium tuum]]. Secondly, that the divine perfection of Christ may appear in you, and so Christ may become known or be declared in you through his glorious effect. [[1:12|and you in him|Et vos in illo]], that is, that you may be glorified in Christ, seeing him in the fatherland face to face[[1 Cor 13:12||]]. Christ, then, is not glorified in us in the same way as we in him. For by his being glorified in us no perfection or glory accrues to him; but by our being glorified in Christ we are perfected in the highest degree. So then may you be glorified in him, [[1:12|according to the grace of our God|secundum gratiam Dei nostri]], that is, according to the measure of grace shown you by the holy Trinity, [[1:12|and of the Lord Jesus Christ|et Domini Jesu Christi]], that is, according to that same grace, which is given us through Christ as mediator and meritorious cause. The Apostle says this lest anyone rely principally on his own merits.

2.title: EXPLANATIO CAPITULI SECUNDI : ROGAMUS AUTEM VOS, FRATRES, ETC.
2.title_en: Explanation of the second chapter: And we beseech you, brethren, etc.

paras.t: Completa gratiarum actione, et oratione pro Thessalonicensibus Deo oblata, in præcedenti capitulo, nunc corrigit errorem eorum, et instruit eos quid de die judicii sit tenendum.
paras.en: Having completed in the preceding chapter the thanksgiving and the prayer offered to God for the Thessalonians, he now corrects their error and instructs them as to what is to be held concerning the day of judgement.

paras.t: Rogamus autem vos, fratres, per adventum Domini nostri Jesu Christi ad extremum judicium, et per adventum nostræ congregationis, id est per collectionem omnium fidelium, in ipsum, id est ad Christum, ad quem omnes in die judicii adducentur. Sic autem rogare, est obsecrare.
paras.en: [[2:1|And we beseech you, brethren, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ|Rogamus autem vos, fratres, per adventum Domini nostri Jesu Christi]] to the last judgement, and by the coming [[2:1|of our gathering together|nostræ congregationis]], that is, by the assembling of all the faithful, [[2:1|unto him|in ipsum]], that is, to Christ, to whom all will be brought on the day of judgement. Now to ask in this way is to entreat [*obsecrare*, to beseech by something sacred].

paras.t: Ut non cito, id est non facile, neque in brevi hora seu modico tempore, moveamini, id est recedatis, a vestro sensu, id est a vero intellectu Scripturæ quem didicistis. Qui enim cito credit, levis est corde. Vel, Non moveamini ad instabilitatem atque errores, a vestro sensu, id est propria sensualitate et naturali ratione, propriis adinventionibus ac imaginationibus potius quam Scripturæ auctoritati intendendo. Neque terreamini vano terrore, arbitrantes instare diem judicii, et persecutiones gravissimas quæ ipsum præcedent. Neque per spiritum, id est, quamvis diabolus se in angelum lucis transfigurans, asserat instare diem novissimum. Neque per sermonem, cujuscumque prædicatoris, neque per epistolam tanquam per nos missam, id est, quamvis aliquis pseudoapostolus miserit vobis epistolam nostro nomine intitulatam: sicut interdum fecerunt pseudoapostoli causa fallendi; quasi instet, id est, in proximo venturus sit, dies Domini, id est tempus finalis judicii.
paras.en: [[2:2|That you be not easily|Ut non cito]], that is, not readily, nor in a short hour or a little time, [[2:2|moved|moveamini]], that is, depart, [[2:2|from your sense|a vestro sensu]], that is, from the true understanding of Scripture which you have learned. For [[Ecclus 19:4|He that is hasty to give credit, is light of heart|Qui enim cito credit, levis est corde]]. Or: Be not [[2:2|moved|moveamini]] to instability and errors [[2:2|from your sense|a vestro sensu]], that is, by your own sensuality and natural reason, attending to your own inventions and imaginings rather than to the authority of Scripture. [[2:2|nor be terrified|Neque terreamini]] with a vain terror, thinking that the day of judgement is at hand, and the most grievous persecutions that will go before it. [[2:2|neither by spirit|Neque per spiritum]], that is, even though the devil, transforming himself into an angel of light, should assert that the last day is at hand. [[2:2|nor by word|Neque per sermonem]] of any preacher whatever, [[2:2|nor by epistle. as sent from us|neque per epistolam tanquam per nos missam]], that is, even though some false apostle should send you a letter entitled with our name, as false apostles sometimes did in order to deceive; [[2:2|as if|quasi]] [[2:2|the day of the Lord|dies Domini]], that is, the time of the final judgement, [[2:2|were at hand|instet]], that is, were to come shortly.

paras.t: Ne quis vos seducat ad hoc æstimandum ullo modo. Error enim et falsitas semper vitanda sunt. Quoniam nisi venerit discessio primum: id est, dies Domini non erit in actu, nec Christus generale judicium faciet, nisi primum, id est ante, venerit discessio gentium a Romano imperio, quæ jam pro magna parte impleta est, vel, discessio particularium Ecclesiarum ab obedientia Romanæ Ecclesiæ. Vel, ut aliis amplius placet, Nisi venerit discessio Christianorum a fide catholica: non quod omnes a fide recedent, sed multi. Dicit enim Salvator, quod tunc abundabit iniquitas, et refrigescet caritas, sicque fides vera in multis deficiet. Propter quod Apostolus alibi dicit: Spiritus manifeste dicit, quia in novissimis diebus discedent quidam a fide. Et Petrus in secunda epistola: Venient in novissimis diebus illusores, juxta proprias concupiscentias ambulantes, et dicentes: Ubi est promissio aut adventus ejus? — Non dicit Apostolus, quod mox venturus sit Christus ad judicium, discessione ista completa, sed quod non veniet nisi ista præcedat. Tamen ista discessione facta, præparata erit via Antichristo, ut recipiatur pene ab omnibus. Idcirco verisimile est quod post discessionem statim veniet Antichristus, vel nascendo, vel publice prædicando, ut aliqui asserunt. Ideo de adventu Antichristi, qui est secundum quod præcedet diem judicii, subditur;
paras.en: [[2:3|Let no man deceive you|Ne quis vos seducat]] into thinking this [[2:3|by any means|ullo modo]]. For error and falsehood are always to be avoided. [[2:3|for unless there come a revolt first|Quoniam nisi venerit discessio primum]]: that is, the day of the Lord will not be in act, nor will Christ hold the general judgement, unless first, that is, before, there come the revolt [*discessio*, a departing or falling away] of the nations from the Roman empire, which is already fulfilled in great part; or the revolt of particular Churches from obedience to the Roman Church. Or, as pleases others more: unless there come the revolt of Christians from the Catholic faith; not that all will fall away from the faith, but many. For the Saviour says that then iniquity will abound and charity grow cold[[Matt 24:12||]], and so the true faith will fail in many. For which reason the Apostle says elsewhere: [[1 Tim 4:1|the Spirit manifestly saith that in the last times some shall depart from the faith|Spiritus manifeste dicit, quia in novissimis diebus discedent quidam a fide]] [Denis has *in the last days*, where the Vulgate has *in the last times*]. And Peter in his second epistle: [[2 Pet 3:3|there shall come deceitful scoffers, walking after their own lusts|Venient in novissimis diebus illusores, juxta proprias concupiscentias ambulantes]], and [[2 Pet 3:4|Saying: Where is his promise or his coming?|dicentes: Ubi est promissio aut adventus ejus?]] — The Apostle does not say that Christ will come to judgement soon, once this revolt is completed, but that he will not come unless it goes before. Yet when this revolt has taken place, the way will have been prepared for Antichrist, so that he is received by almost all. It is therefore likely that Antichrist will come straight after the revolt, either by being born or by preaching publicly, as some assert. And so, of the coming of Antichrist, which is the second thing that will go before the day of judgement, it is added:

paras.t: Et revelatus fuerit, id est manifestatus mundo, imo se ipsum hominibus manifestaverit, homo peccati, filius perditionis, id est Antichristus, per excellentiam homo peccati vocatus, tanquam omnibus vitiis præ cunctis hominibus plenus, et ceteris quasi fons et origo peccandi exsistens, ad æternam damnationem seu perditionem immoderatissime tendens: qui adversatur, id est, Christo adversabitur ac toti Ecclesiæ, et extollitur, id est, per superbiam erigetur, supra omne quod dicitur Deus, id est, universis creaturis (quæ vel singulari perfectione, vel vana hominum opinione dii vocantur) se præferet, aut quod colitur, id est, etiam per tumorem elationis gravissime supra verum Deum extolletur: non quod dicturus sit se Deo majorem, sed quoniam Deum nil prorsus timebit, atque divinæ voluntati suam in omnibus præferet, divinum cultum exterminans, et suum inducens. Cujus figura fuit, quod de Nabuchodonosor scribitur, qui Holoferni præcepit omnes deos terræ exterminari, ut ipse solus a suis subditis, imo ab omnibus coleretur ut deus, et deus vocaretur. Ita ut Antichristus in templo Dei sedeat, ostendens se suis cultoribus tanquam sit Deus: nam et Deum et Dei Filium se vocabit. Per templum vero in quo sessurus est, intelligitur templum quod ipse cum Judæis sibi adhærentibus (ut fertur) in Jerusalem ædificabit.
paras.en: And [[2:3|be revealed|revelatus fuerit]], that is, made manifest to the world, nay, shall have manifested himself to men, [[2:3|the man of sin|homo peccati]], [[2:3|the son of perdition|filius perditionis]], that is, Antichrist, called the man of sin by pre-eminence, as being full of all vices beyond all other men, and being as it were the fount and origin of sinning for the rest, tending most immoderately to eternal damnation or perdition: [[2:4|Who opposeth|qui adversatur]], that is, will oppose Christ and the whole Church, [[2:4|and is lifted up|et extollitur]], that is, will be raised up by pride, [[2:4|above all that is called God|supra omne quod dicitur Deus]], that is, will set himself above all creatures (which are called gods either for a singular perfection or by the vain opinion of men), [[2:4|or that is worshipped|aut quod colitur]], that is, by the swelling of his pride he will lift himself up most grievously even above the true God: not that he will say he is greater than God, but because he will fear God not at all, and will set his own will above the divine will in all things, rooting out the worship of God and bringing in his own. A figure of this was what is written of Nabuchodonosor, who commanded Holofernes to destroy all the gods of the earth, so that he alone should be worshipped as a god by his subjects, nay, by all, and be called god [this is Judith 3:13]. [[2:4|so that he sitteth in the temple of God|Ita ut Antichristus in templo Dei sedeat]], [[2:4|shewing himself|ostendens se]] to his worshippers [[2:4|as if he were God|tanquam sit Deus]]: for he will call himself both God and the Son of God. By the temple in which he is to sit is understood the temple which he, with the Jews who cleave to him, will build (as is reported) in Jerusalem.

paras.t: Non retinetis memoriter, quod quum adhuc essem apud vos corporali præsentia in vestri conversione, hæc quæ nunc scribo de discessione et Antichristo ac die judicii, dicebam vobis proprio ore? Et nunc quid detineat, id est, Antichristi adventum differat, scitis, videlicet quia discessio nondum completa est, nec tempus divinitus præstitutum seu præordinatum adventui Antichristi advenit. Hoc igitur detinet, sic tamen, ut reveletur homo peccati in suo tempore, id est divinitus prædisposito. Revelabitur enim aliquando, quod patet ex hoc: Nam mysterium jam operatur iniquitatis, id est, diabolus per Neronem et alios tyrannos, tempore isto, facit peccata præfigurativa malitiæ Antichristi. Persecutio quippe Neronis et aliorum similium occidentium Christianos, præfiguravit persecutionem ab Antichristo fidelibus infligendam. Et sicut Nero occidit Petrum et Paulum, sic Antichristus occidet Enoch atque Eliam. Denique, sicut Abel, Joseph, David, Samson et alii multi, Christi figuræ fuerunt, sic Nero, Simon magus, Antiochus Illustris, Diocletianus, Antichristi erant figuræ. Vel sic, et redit quasi in idem: Nam mysterium iniquitatis, id est iniquitas mysterialis occulta et figurativa iniquitatis in Antichristo futuræ, jam operatur in Nerone, cæterisque prædictis, qui nunc talia operantur contra Christum et sanctos, qualia tunc operabitur Antichristus.
paras.en: [[2:5|Remember you not|Non retinetis]] in memory [[2:5|that, when I was yet with you|quod quum adhuc essem apud vos]] in bodily presence at your conversion, [[2:5|I told you|dicebam vobis]] with my own mouth [[2:5|these things|hæc]] which I now write about the revolt and Antichrist and the day of judgement? [[2:6|And now|Et nunc]] [[2:6|what withholdeth|quid detineat]], that is, delays the coming of Antichrist, [[2:6|you know|scitis]]: namely, that the revolt is not yet complete, and the time divinely appointed or foreordained for the coming of Antichrist has not yet arrived. This then withholds, yet in such a way [[2:6|that he may be revealed|ut reveletur]], the man of sin, [[2:6|in his time|in suo tempore]], that is, the time divinely disposed beforehand. For he will be revealed at some time, as is plain from this: [[2:7|For the mystery of iniquity already worketh|Nam mysterium jam operatur iniquitatis]], that is, the devil, through Nero and other tyrants, at this time works sins that prefigure the malice of Antichrist. For the persecution of Nero and of others like him who slew Christians prefigured the persecution that Antichrist will inflict on the faithful. And as Nero slew Peter and Paul, so Antichrist will slay Enoch and Elias. And indeed, as Abel, Joseph, David, Samson and many others were figures of Christ, so Nero, Simon Magus, Antiochus the Illustrious [that is, Antiochus Epiphanes], Diocletian were figures of Antichrist. Or thus, and it comes to much the same: [[2:7|For the mystery of iniquity|Nam mysterium iniquitatis]], that is, a mystical iniquity, hidden and figurative of the iniquity to come in Antichrist, [[2:7|already worketh|jam operatur]] in Nero and the others aforesaid, who now work such things against Christ and the saints as Antichrist will work then.

paras.t: Hoc loco ait B. Hieronymus: Quod Apostolus dixerit sciri a Thessalonicensibus, non exponit hoc loco aperte. Ideo nos qui nescimus quod illi sciebant, pervenire cum labore ad id quod sensit Apostolus, cupimus, nec valemus: præsertim quoniam verba sequentia hunc sensum faciunt obscuriorem. Quid enim est quod subditur, Tantum ut qui tenet nunc, teneat, donec de medio fiat? Denique circa hæc verba Augustinus fatetur: Ego prorsus ignoro quid dixerit. — Glossa tamen exponit hunc locum variis modis, quorum unus: Mysterium iniquitatis jam operatur (secundum sensus inductos); tantum hoc restat implendum, antequam filius perditionis appareat, ut qui tenet nunc, id est homo jam tenens Romanum imperium, teneat illud, id est, qui imperat, imperet, donec ipsa Romani imperii potestas de medio fiat, id est, penitus deleatur. Nam ante adventum Antichristi cessabit, ut dicitur. Vel sic, Ut qui tenet fidem, teneat eam donec ipsa fides de medio fiat, id est, tollatur quantum ad plurimos, sicut expositum est.
paras.en: On this place Blessed Jerome says [the margin has *Augustinus*: these words are Augustine's, in the City of God, XX, 19]: What the Apostle said was known to the Thessalonians, he does not set out openly in this place. And so we, who do not know what they knew, desire to reach with labour what the Apostle meant, and cannot; especially since the words that follow make this sense more obscure. For what is it that is added, [[2:7|only that he who now holdeth do hold, until he be taken out of the way|Tantum ut qui tenet nunc, teneat, donec de medio fiat]]? And indeed Augustine confesses concerning these words: I am wholly ignorant of what he meant. — The Gloss, however, expounds this place in various ways, of which one is: [[2:7|the mystery of iniquity already worketh|Mysterium iniquitatis jam operatur]] (according to the senses brought forward); only this remains to be fulfilled before the son of perdition appears, [[2:7|that he who now holdeth|ut qui tenet nunc]], that is, the man now holding the Roman empire, [[2:7|do hold|teneat]] it, that is, that he who rules, rule, until the power of the Roman empire itself [[2:7|be taken out of the way|de medio fiat]], that is, be utterly destroyed. For it will cease before the coming of Antichrist, as is said. Or thus: that he who holds the faith, hold it, until the faith itself be taken out of the way, that is, be taken away as far as the greater number are concerned, as has been explained.

paras.t: Et tunc, id est discessione hac triplici consummata, revelabitur, id est, se ipsum ostendet et regnare incipiet, ille iniquus, quem Dominus Jesus interficiet spiritu oris sui, id est suo præcepto jubens eum occidi a Michaele, vel per se ipsum eum occidens suo adspectu. Unde apud Danielem de Antichristo conscriptum est: Sine manu conteretur. Quidam etiam dicunt quod fulminabitur. Hinc et in Isaia legitur: Spiritu labiorum suorum interficiet impium. Quidam per spiritum oris Christi, intelligunt Spiritum Sanctum, cujus virtute occidendus est Antichristus. Et destruet illustratione adventus sui eum, id est, Dominus Jesus conteret et damnabit Antichristum cum suis, suo claro adventu ad judicium, quando dicturus est: Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum.
paras.en: [[2:8|And then|Et tunc]], that is, when this threefold revolt has been consummated, [[2:8|shall be revealed|revelabitur]], that is, shall show himself and begin to reign, [[2:8|that wicked one|ille iniquus]], [[2:8|whom the Lord Jesus shall kill with the spirit of his mouth|quem Dominus Jesus interficiet spiritu oris sui]], that is, by his command, ordering him to be slain by Michael; or slaying him himself by his look. Hence in Daniel it is written of Antichrist: He [[Dan 8:25|shall be broken without hand|Sine manu conteretur]] [the margin gives Dan. vii, 25; the words are Dan 8:25]. Some also say that he will be struck by lightning. Hence too we read in Isaias: [[Is 11:4|with the breath of his lips he shall slay the wicked|Spiritu labiorum suorum interficiet impium]] [*spiritus*, spirit or breath]. Some understand by the spirit of Christ's mouth the Holy Ghost, by whose power Antichrist is to be slain. [[2:8|and shall destroy with the brightness of his coming: him|Et destruet illustratione adventus sui eum]], that is, the Lord Jesus will crush and condemn Antichrist with his followers by his glorious coming to judgement, when he will say: [[Matt 25:41|Depart from me, you cursed, into everlasting fire|Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum]] [Denis has *Go*, where the Vulgate has *Depart from me*].

paras.t: Cujus est adventus secundum operationem Satanæ. Duplex ponitur Antichristi adventus: primus, occultus, qui pertinet ad ejus generationem; alter, manifestus, pertinens ad ejus prædicationem, de quo jam tractat Apostolus. Adventus ergo, id est manifestatio Antichristi, qua se hominibus ostendet tanquam verum Christum ac Filium Dei, est, id est, erit (loquitur enim Apostolus more prophetico de futuro per modum præsentis), secundum operationem Satanæ, id est dæmone cooperante, in omni virtute potestatis humanæ. Maximam enim habebit multitudinem ministrorum, et omnibus divitiis abundabit, nec erit qui ei poterit humana virtute resistere. Et signis, quantum ad miracula minora, et prodigiis, quantum ad majora, mendacibus, id est apparentibus, vel ad fallendum ordinatis.
paras.en: [[2:9|Whose coming is according to the working of Satan|Cujus est adventus secundum operationem Satanæ]]. A twofold coming of Antichrist is set down: the first hidden, which belongs to his generation; the other manifest, belonging to his preaching, of which the Apostle now treats. The coming, then, that is, the manifestation of Antichrist, by which he will show himself to men as the true Christ and Son of God, [[2:9|is|est]], that is, will be (for the Apostle, in the manner of the prophets, speaks of the future as if it were present), [[2:9|according to the working of Satan|secundum operationem Satanæ]], that is, with the devil working with him, [[2:9|in all power|in omni virtute]] of human might. For he will have a very great multitude of ministers, and abound in all riches, and there will be none able to resist him by human power. [[2:9|and signs|Et signis]], as to the lesser miracles, and [[2:9|wonders|prodigiis]], as to the greater, [[2:9|lying|mendacibus]], that is, apparent, or ordained to deceive.

paras.t: Solet autem quæri, an Antichristus et ejus ministri vera miracula facient. Et respondendum, quod si de miraculis propriissime loquamur, videlicet tanquam de effectibus totam naturalem facultatem ac ordinem rerum transcendentibus, tunc non facient miracula vere, sed solum apparenter, et in præstigiis illudendo sensus humanos. Nempe talia fieri nequeunt nisi virtute divina: de quibus ait Psalmographus, Benedictus Dominus Deus Israel, qui facit mirabilia solus. Talia fecit Christus, sicut ait: Si opera non fecissem in eis quæ nemo alius fecit, peccatum non haberent. Si autem loquamur de miraculis magis communiter, velut de effectibus inconsuetis et præter solitum cursum naturalemque modum productis, sic facient vera miracula adjuvante diabolo. Unde in Apocalypsi legitur: Dedit illi draco virtutem et potestatem magnam; et rursus: Fecit signa magna, ut etiam ignem faceret de cœlo descendere in conspectu hominum, et seducet habitantes in terra propter signa quæ data sunt illi. Hoc et Christus in Evangelio testatur: Surgent, inquiens, pseudochristi, et dabunt signa magna, ita ut in errorem ducantur, si fieri potest, etiam electi. Dicuntur tamen miracula ista mendacia, non formaliter, sed finaliter, quia ad fallendum seu falsitatum confirmationem ordinabuntur. Aliqua autem erunt omnino mendacia sive phantasmata, ad illudendum hominibus.
paras.en: Now it is commonly asked whether Antichrist and his ministers will work true miracles. And the answer is that if we speak of miracles in the most proper sense, namely as effects that surpass the whole power of nature and the order of things, then they will not work miracles truly, but only in appearance, mocking the senses of men with illusions. For such things cannot be done except by divine power; of these the Psalmist says: [[Ps 71:18|Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, who alone doth wonderful things|Benedictus Dominus Deus Israel, qui facit mirabilia solus]]. Such things Christ did, as he says: [[John 15:24|If I had not done among them the works that no other man hath done, they would not have sin|Si opera non fecissem in eis quæ nemo alius fecit, peccatum non haberent]]. But if we speak of miracles more commonly, as of effects that are unusual and produced beyond the wonted course and natural manner, then they will work true miracles with the devil's help. Hence we read in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 13:2|the dragon gave him his own strength and great power|Dedit illi draco virtutem et potestatem magnam]]; and again: [[Apoc 13:13|And he did great signs, so that he made also fire to come down from heaven unto the earth, in the sight of men|Fecit signa magna, ut etiam ignem faceret de cœlo descendere in conspectu hominum]], [[Apoc 13:14|And he seduced them that dwell on the earth, for the signs which were given him|et seducet habitantes in terra propter signa quæ data sunt illi]] [Denis has *he will seduce*]. Christ too bears witness to this in the Gospel: [[Matt 24:24|there shall arise|Surgent]], he says, [[Matt 24:24|false Christs and false prophets and shall shew great signs and wonders, insomuch as to deceive (if possible) even the elect|pseudochristi, et dabunt signa magna, ita ut in errorem ducantur, si fieri potest, etiam electi]]. Yet these miracles are called lying not formally but finally [that is, not in what they are but in the end they serve], because they will be ordained to deceive, or to confirm falsehoods. Some, however, will be wholly lying, or phantoms, to mock men.

paras.t: Et in omni seductione iniquitatis, id est in omni genere deceptionis injustæ ad iniquitatem trahentis, iis qui pereunt, id est ad damnationem reproborum. Variis autem modis Antichristus decipiet mundum, videlicet simulatione sanctitatis, Scripturarum allegationibus, sapientia et ornatu sermonis, eminentia miraculorum, promissione divitiarum, terrore minarum, potestate, prosperitate, ac multitudine ministrorum suorum. Sic ergo veniet reprobis, eo quod caritatem veritatis, id est veram dilectionem, seu Christi, qui veritas est, amorem, non receperunt, perseverando in ea ut salvi fierent, promerendo vitam æternam, ad quam sola perseverantia ducit. Ideo, id est in pœnam hujus peccati, mittet permissive illis Deus operationem erroris, id est fallacias Antichristi, ut credant mendacio, id est falsæ doctrinæ Antichristi. Tenetur autem hic dictio, Ut, consecutive, non causaliter.
paras.en: [[2:10|And in all seduction of iniquity|Et in omni seductione iniquitatis]], that is, in every kind of unjust deceit that draws to iniquity, [[2:10|to them that perish|iis qui pereunt]], that is, to the damnation of the reprobate. Now Antichrist will deceive the world in various ways: by a show of holiness, by citing the Scriptures, by wisdom and eloquence of speech, by the eminence of his miracles, by promises of riches, by the terror of threats, by power, by prosperity, and by the multitude of his ministers. So then he will come to the reprobate, [[2:10|because|eo quod]] [[2:10|the love of the truth|caritatem veritatis]], that is, true love, or the love of Christ, who is the truth[[John 14:6||]], they [[2:10|receive not|non receperunt]], by persevering in it, [[2:10|that they might be saved|ut salvi fierent]], by meriting eternal life, to which perseverance alone leads[[Matt 24:13||]]. [[2:10|Therefore|Ideo]], that is, in punishment of this sin, [[2:10|God shall send them|mittet permissive illis Deus]] [*permissive*, that is, by permitting it] [[2:10|the operation of error|operationem erroris]], that is, the deceits of Antichrist, [[2:10|to believe lying|ut credant mendacio]], that is, the false teaching of Antichrist. Here the word *ut* [*that*, *so as to*] is taken of the consequence, not of the cause.

paras.t: Ut judicentur, id est, ab electis discernantur, ad sinistram ponantur et condemnentur, omnes qui non crediderunt fide formata ac stabili, veritati evangelicæ legis, sed consenserunt iniquitati doctrinæ et operum Antichristi.
paras.en: [[2:11|That all may be judged|Ut judicentur]], that is, be separated from the elect, set on the left hand and condemned, [[2:11|who have not believed|omnes qui non crediderunt]][[Mark 16:16||]] with a formed and steadfast faith [*fides formata*, that is, faith informed by charity], [[2:11|the truth|veritati]] of the law of the Gospel, [[2:11|but have consented to iniquity|sed consenserunt iniquitati]] of the teaching and works of Antichrist.

paras.t: Nos autem pastores vestri, debemus debito condescentiæ vel caritate exigente, gratias agere Deo semper pro vobis, id est vice vestra, vel pro beneficiis vobis collatis, o fratres dilecti a Deo: quibus convenit illud Joannis, Nos ergo diligamus Deum, quoniam ipse prior dilexit nos; quod elegerit vos Deus, id est, ab æterno prædestinaverit, primitias, id est ad hoc ut essetis primi de Christifidelibus, in salutem, id est ad obtinendam felicitatem æternam. Erant enim Thessalonicenses de primitiva Ecclesia. In sanctificatione spiritus, id est in infusione gratiæ Spiritus Sancti, seu Baptismo ubi Spiritus Sanctus datur et homo sanctificatur ad obtinendam salutem, et fide veritatis, id est fide catholica data a Christo, qui est veritas prima. Nam per sanctificationem istam et fidem acquiritur salus æterna, ad quam pertinet divina electio.
paras.en: [[2:12|But we|Nos autem]], your pastors, [[2:12|ought|debemus]], by a debt of condescension, or as charity requires, [[2:12|to give thanks to God always for you|gratias agere Deo semper pro vobis]], that is, in your stead, or for the benefits bestowed on you, O [[2:12|brethren, beloved of God|fratres dilecti a Deo]]: to whom that saying of John fits: [[1 John 4:19|Let us therefore love God: because God first hath loved us|Nos ergo diligamus Deum, quoniam ipse prior dilexit nos]]; [[2:12|for that God hath chosen you|quod elegerit vos Deus]], that is, predestined you from eternity, [[2:12|firstfruits|primitias]], that is, to this, that you should be among the first of the faithful of Christ, [[2:12|unto salvation|in salutem]], that is, to obtain eternal happiness. For the Thessalonians belonged to the primitive Church. [[2:12|in sanctification of the spirit|In sanctificatione spiritus]], that is, in the infusion of the grace of the Holy Ghost, or in Baptism, where the Holy Ghost is given and man is sanctified to obtain salvation, [[2:12|and faith of the truth|et fide veritatis]], that is, the Catholic faith given by Christ, who is the first truth[[John 14:6||]]. For by this sanctification and faith eternal salvation is gained, to which the divine election belongs.

paras.t: In quam, id est ad quam veram fidem, et vocavit vos Deus vocatione suæ inspirationis internæ, per evangelium nostrum, id est per prædicationem sancti Evangelii a nobis exhibitam, qua admoniti estis ad fidei susceptionem: quam et Deus vobis infudit, in acquisitionem gloriæ, id est ad adipiscendam beatitudinem, Domini nostri Jesu Christi: qui ait, Qui credit in me, habet vitam æternam; itemque, Beati qui non viderunt et crediderunt.
paras.en: [[2:13|Whereunto|In quam]], that is, to which true faith, [[2:13|also he hath called you|et vocavit vos]], God, by the call of his inward inspiration, [[2:13|by our gospel|per evangelium nostrum]], that is, by the preaching of the holy Gospel set before you by us, by which you were moved to receive the faith, which God also infused into you, [[2:13|unto the purchasing of the glory|in acquisitionem gloriæ]], that is, to obtain beatitude, [[2:13|of our Lord Jesus Christ|Domini nostri Jesu Christi]], who says: [[John 6:47|He that believeth in me hath everlasting life|Qui credit in me, habet vitam æternam]]; and again: [[John 20:29|blessed are they that have not seen and have believed|Beati qui non viderunt et crediderunt]].

paras.t: Itaque, fratres, state in gratia, non ruentes in vitia; et tenete traditiones, id est, morales instructiones seu jussiones implete, quas didicistis, sive per sermonem vocalem oris nostri, sive per epistolam nostram præsentem seu præcedentem.
paras.en: [[2:14|Therefore, brethren, stand fast|Itaque, fratres, state]] in grace, not falling into vices; [[2:14|and hold the traditions|et tenete traditiones]], that is, fulfil the moral instructions or commands, [[2:14|which you have learned, whether by word|quas didicistis, sive per sermonem]] spoken by our mouth, [[2:14|or by our epistle|sive per epistolam nostram]], this present one or the preceding one.

paras.t: Ipse autem Dominus noster Jesus Christus, et Deus Pater noster, id est Trinitas vel persona Patris, qui est Deus creatione, et pater gubernatione ac dilectione, qui dilexit nos ab æterno, quemadmodum beneficia ejus testantur: nam et propter nimiam caritatem suam qua dilexit nos, Filium suum misit in similitudinem carnis peccati; et dedit nobis consolationem æternam, nunc in spe et per quamdam inchoationem, frequenter nos lætificando, nostram redemptionem annuntiando, futura præmia proponendo ac promittendo, imo et in omni tribulatione nostra nos consolando. Hanc consolationem æternam daturus est tandem in re, et per felicem consummationem. Propter quod ait Christus discipulis suis: Iterum videbo vos, et gaudium vestrum nemo tollet a vobis. Ideo subditur: et spem bonam in gratia, id est, per gratiam suam præstitit nobis certam ac piam fiduciam adipiscendi consolationem prædictam, sicuti Christus loquitur: Petite, et accipietis, ut gaudium vestrum sit plenum; exhortetur, id est, gratiose excitet, corda vestra, et confirmet ea in omni opere et sermone bono, id est meritorio.
paras.en: [[2:15|Now our Lord Jesus Christ himself|Ipse autem Dominus noster Jesus Christus]], [[2:15|and God and our Father|et Deus Pater noster]], that is, the Trinity, or the person of the Father, who is God by creation, and Father by governance and love, [[2:15|who hath loved us|qui dilexit nos]] from eternity, as his benefits bear witness: indeed, [[Eph 2:4|for his exceeding charity wherewith he loved us|propter nimiam caritatem suam qua dilexit nos]] he sent his own Son [[Rom 8:3|in the likeness of sinful flesh|in similitudinem carnis peccati]]; [[2:15|and hath given us everlasting consolation|et dedit nobis consolationem æternam]], now in hope and by a certain beginning, often gladdening us, announcing our redemption, setting before us and promising rewards to come, nay, comforting us [[2 Cor 1:4|in all our tribulation|in omni tribulatione nostra]]. This eternal consolation he will at last give in reality, and by a happy consummation. For which reason Christ says to his disciples: [[John 16:22|I will see you again|Iterum videbo vos]], [[John 16:22|And your joy no man shall take from you|et gaudium vestrum nemo tollet a vobis]]. And so it is added: [[2:15|and good hope in grace|et spem bonam in gratia]], that is, by his grace he has granted us a sure and loving confidence of obtaining the aforesaid consolation, as Christ says: [[John 16:24|Ask, and you shall receive; that your joy may be full|Petite, et accipietis, ut gaudium vestrum sit plenum]]; [[2:16|Exhort|exhortetur]], that is, graciously stir up, [[2:16|your hearts|corda vestra]], [[2:16|and confirm you|et confirmet]] them [[2:16|in every good work and word|in omni opere et sermone bono]], that is, meritorious.
